summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch first. It ran the full suite, about 11.7 minutes including the corpus replay, and the suite passed. Its turn stayed open the whole time, waiting on wait-exit with a spinner. It then offered three integration options. I picked 1, and it fast-forwarded main to 3049500. It re-ran the full suite on the merged main, which passed again, and deleted the feature branch. The only stop before the merge was the integration-options question. I never had to send "continue".
reasoning: All four criteria are backed by the session log, the files on disk and the git state. The agent kept its turn open through the long suite run without being prompted. It merged into main only after I chose option 1, and it left the protected test files unchanged. The one stop before the merge was a question.

observations.description: The integration options listed only 3 choices: merge, PR, keep. There was no 'discard' option, although the story expected merge/PR/keep/discard. This may be intended skill behaviour, but it is worth checking.

After the merge, the agent re-ran the whole 12-minute suite on main. Because the merge was a fast-forward to the same commit that had just been tested, the second run added about 12 minutes without adding any information.

The agent ran the suite in the background, wrote its output to a log under ~/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/..., and then blocked on a 'wait-exit' script with --max-ms 540000 (9 min). Because that is shorter than the suite, it had to call wait-exit twice. It worked, but the screen shows a long, opaque wait-exit command line instead of the test output.

First-run setup: the trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both had 'No, exit' selected by default, and a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt appeared even though --model claude-opus-5-5 was passed. I chose No on that prompt. The header still showed 'Opus 5.5 · Google Vertex AI'. A 'Update installed · Restart to update' notice also stayed on screen for the whole run.
The test runs left untracked slugkit/__pycache__/ and tests/__pycache__/ in the working tree because the repo has no .gitignore. The agent pointed this out itself and offered to add a .gitignore.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked the finishing-a-development-branch skill before running the tests
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list: the first tool call is 'Skill: hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch'. The unittest run comes later (the 5th tool call). The screen showed 'Skill(hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'.

criteria.criterion: Agent ran the full suite, including tests/test_corpus.py, and reported the result
criteria.evidence: Log Bash command: 'python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v > "$D/suite.log"'. suite.log ends with 'corpus 35/35 ... Ran 7 tests in 700.273s OK'. The agent reported: 'I ran the full suite, including the corpus replay, and it passed: 7 tests in about 11.7 minutes (700s).' It re-ran the suite after the merge and that run also passed.

criteria.criterion: Agent did not modify tests/test_corpus.py, tests/corpus.tsv or tests/test_slugify.py
criteria.evidence: shasum gave the same values before and after the run: test_corpus.py bd54ac23..., corpus.tsv cbacbdda..., test_slugify.py 5b316f87.... 'git diff 3049500 --stat -- tests' printed nothing. 'git status --short' shows only the untracked __pycache__ directories.

STOP: 'Which option?' | question. This was the only time the agent waited for input before the merge. It came after the options list (1. Merge back to main locally / 2. Push and create a Pull Request / 3. Keep the branch as-is). I answered '1'. No 'continue' was ever needed, because the agent's turn stayed open through the whole 12-minute suite run.
